forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Uttlesford expects to use reserves from 2026/27 as funding falls
news_drafts.lead: Uttlesford achieved a £0.854m underspend in 2025/26 without drawing on reserves, but the council now expects to use its reserves from 2026/27 onwards to cover projected deficits caused by reduced government funding following the Fair Funding Review. The council holds sufficient reserves to cover these deficits and is pursuing efficiency savings through its Blueprint 2.0 programme, targeting £900,000 in 2026/27 and £2.5m by 2030/31. However, the Audit and Standards Committee heard that 33 audit recommendations now remain overdue, including one critical priority item. Housing has been a persistent area of concern, with the audit identifying control weaknesses in an £8.6m maintenance contract, including undocumented payment discrepancies, and unresolved recommendations on debt recovery and project management that date back over a year.

findings.headline: The 2026-27 audit portfolio includes 2 critical-level and 28 high-priority findings among 76 total recommendations.
findings.detail: Internal audits conducted in 2026-27 identified recommendations across severity levels: 2 critical, 28 high, 40 medium, and 6 low priority. The presence of critical and high-priority findings indicates material weaknesses in governance and control systems that require urgent remediation.
findings.matters: Critical and high-priority audit findings indicate material control environment deficiencies; lenders assess these as risk factors affecting financial reporting reliability and operational governance.
findings.figures: 2 Critical, 28 High, 40 Medium, 6 Low priority findings

findings.headline: As of 31 August 2026, 33 audit recommendations are overdue, including one critical-priority finding.
findings.detail: Of 76 audit recommendations tracked for 2026-27, only 23 have been closed by 31 August 2026. Thirty-three remain overdue, containing 1 critical, 9 high, 21 medium, and 2 low-priority items. This 43% overdue rate indicates the council is significantly behind on implementing audit-identified improvements.
findings.matters: Lenders and finance directors assess recommendation closure rates as a gauge of governance response; high overdue rates signal weak internal control environment management and weak follow-up discipline.
findings.figures: 33 overdue (1 Critical, 9 High, 21 Medium, 2 Low); 23 closed from 76 total

findings.headline: Contract management control audit assigned MODERATE ASSURANCE due to gaps in practical guidance, with high-priority recommendation to strengthen manager training and templates.
findings.detail: Internal audit of the council's post-award contract management arrangements found MODERATE ASSURANCE. The audit identified a high-priority recommendation to provide more detailed guidance, training and templates for managers, noting that while a Contract Management Framework was created in September 2024, it lacks practical guidance on what contract management work should be conducted, how checks should be performed, and how work should be documented and evidenced. Three medium-priority recommendations address enhancing performance management, improving contract register accuracy, and completing the contract library.
findings.matters: Contract management is fundamental to value for money in council spending; an audit weakness indicates the council's financial controls are not yet mature and contract management practice may be inconsistent across the organisation.
findings.figures: MODERATE ASSURANCE overall opinion; 1 high-priority recommendation; 3 medium-priority recommendations
findings.quote: A high-priority recommendation has been raised to provide more detailed guidance, training and templates for managers.

findings.paper_title: Uttlesford District Council 2025-26 Rebuilding Assurance Update report
findings.headline: Rebuild audit work extends to 2027/28 with additional costs of £93,000–£115,000
findings.detail: KPMG's risk assessment phase costs £63,000–£75,000 and the substantive phase £30,000–£40,000, subject to PSAA variation. The capacity assessment timetable shows potential completion dates extending to 2027/28, meaning the council will not return to a clean, unmodified audit opinion until fiscal year 2027/28 at the earliest.
findings.matters: The lender needs confidence that the council is moving toward normal audit status. An extended rebuild to 2027/28 (three+ more years) and substantial additional costs signal that audit recovery will be a prolonged process.
findings.quote: We note our fees for the risk assessment phase of work are expected to be £63,000-£75,000. We estimate the fees for the substantive phase are £30,000-£40,000.

findings.paper_title: Uttlesford District Council 2025-26 Rebuilding Assurance Update report
findings.headline: Split between useable and unusable reserves still unaudited as at 31 March 2025, described as pervasive to financial position
findings.detail: Despite rebuilding work, KPMG could not obtain sufficient audit evidence to verify the split between useable and unusable reserves for 31 March 2025 or 31 March 2024 before the statutory backstop deadline. The auditor states this gap is 'pervasive' — meaning it affects the overall picture of the council's financial position — and deferred resolution to the 2025/26 audit.
findings.matters: The useable/unusable split is fundamental: it determines how much discretionary cash the council actually has available. This cannot be confirmed, representing a gap in the lender's understanding of liquidity.
findings.figures: Gap applies to both 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024
findings.quote: Given our work to rebuild assurance is not complete and due to the statutory backstop date of 27 February 2026, we have determined that there is insufficient time to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence over the split of useable and unusable reserves as at 31 March 2025 or 31 March 2024 ahead of the backstop, and, in our view, this is pervasive to the Council's and the Group's financial position as at 31 March 2025.
